title: Reentrancy via ERC1155 callback causes inner forceApprove(0) to clobber outer batch's allowance, atomic rollback
description: A smart-contract recipient implementing onERC1155Received that re-enters batchMint(...) reaches line 81's forceApprove(nftMinter, 0) on the inner call, revoking the outer call's still-active allowance. Outer's next iteration's mint() reverts. Whole tx atomically reverts — DoS only, no theft. Caller controls recipient (self-inflicted). Project documents intentional absence of reentrancy guards; this finding refines that with a concrete DoS path and recommends adding nonReentrant for cheap defense-in-depth.
recommendation: Add OpenZeppelin's nonReentrant modifier to batchMint() for cheap defense-in-depth. Alternative: track and restore previous allowance instead of forceApprove(0) on cleanup.
